summary.headline: Carborundum Q2 FY27 standalone sales rose 28% YoY to INR 911 crores, a record, while consolidated PAT fell to INR 12 crores on INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items.
summary.overview: Standalone sales hit a record INR 911 crores (+28% YoY, +7.7% QoQ), with all three segments growing double digits in H1. Consolidated sales rose 13.1% YoY to INR 1,455 crores, but consolidated PAT after NCI fell to INR 12 crores from INR 75 crores, driven by INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items linked to AWUKO closure and Foskor Zirconia. Management raised FY27 Ceramics guidance to 25-28% growth and margin to 22.5-23.5%, but cut Abrasives margin guidance to 8-8.5% excluding AWUKO. Operating cash flow was weak in H1 on working capital build, which management expects to reverse in H2.

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: Sales INR 313 crores (+37.2% YoY, +14% QoQ); PBIT INR 67 crores (+48.2% YoY). Growth led by Engineered Ceramics and Metallized Cylinders, with refractories also contributing.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: Sales INR 279 crores (+31.3% YoY, flat QoQ); PBIT INR 29 crores (+49.1% YoY, down 24% QoQ from INR 39 crores). Management cited product and industry mix for the QoQ margin drop.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: Sales INR 357 crores (+15.9% YoY, +8.6% QoQ); PBIT INR 37 crores (-19.9% YoY), margin around 10%. Cost pressure from phenolic resins and oil-linked inputs, with only a small pass-through.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: Sales INR 410 crores (+36.1% YoY, +17.6% QoQ); PBIT INR 101 crores (+62.1% YoY). Growth across India, Americas and Australia.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: Sales INR 443 crores (+11.1% YoY, -6.3% QoQ) due to lower Foskor Zirconia sales; PBIT INR 26 crores (-20.9% YoY).

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: Sales INR 607 crores (+4% YoY); PBIT INR 40 crores (+20.8% YoY). RHODIUS sales EUR 14.5 million (-16.8% YoY) with loss of EUR 0.3 million; AWUKO sales EUR 1.1 million vs EUR 2.9 million.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Q2 sales RUB 1.55 billion, flat YoY; PAT RUB 98.7 million vs RUB 222 million a year earlier, up from RUB 52.1 million in Q1.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia
segments.commentary: Under closure as commercially unviable; Q2 sales ZAR 53 million and loss of ZAR 24 million.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth FY27 approx 4-4.5% as reported; 11-12% excluding Foskor and AWUKO (INR 343 crores in FY26). Revised earlier guidance of 15% retained.
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth raised to 25-28% (from 23-25%); Ceramics margin raised to 22.5-23.5% (from 20.5-21%).
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth 5.5-6% as reported, 11-12% excluding AWUKO (about INR 108 crores). Abrasives margin 8-8.5% excluding AWUKO, down from 9.5-10% guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales decline 6.5-7% as reported; 8-9% ex-Foskor. Prior 9-10% revision retained. Margin guidance 9-9.5% retained.
Consolidated capex guidance of INR 400 crores retained.
RHODIUS: FY27 sales now expected flat YoY (previously +5%), with a smaller loss than FY26; breakeven targeted by Q1 FY28.
Semiconductor equipment components segment: top line of INR 300-350 crores expected around FY30-31; segment margins to be above the 20-21% baseline in a stable state.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR 127 crores vs INR 162 crores in H1 FY26; FY27 consolidated capex guidance INR 400 crores retained.
Semiconductor equipment components: anchor customer; about INR 66 crores capex already incurred; total investment could scale to 3-4x current level; revenues from FY28, peak by FY30.

Armor line capex of about INR 50 crores mentioned; electronic substrate (AMB/DBC) program in trials, first articles expected this year; management said at least a year before completion and gave no revenue figure.
Hosur thin wheel facility established to absorb the Uttarakhand thin wheel operations; qualification under way with 6-7 major international customers.
AWUKO sold property, plant, equipment and inventory for INR 5.34 crores; liquidation and de-registration in progress. Foskor exit expected to be completed in the current quarter, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was mainly volume-driven, with a small price contribution; demand supported by industrial, construction and infrastructure activity.
Abrasives cost pressure from phenolic resins and oil-linked inputs; only a small portion passed to market, with management calling it largely timing. Management expects margins to recover toward 15%.
Ceramics exports are about 85%+ of sales; growth led by Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders, while wear ceramics also grew.
Refractories: demand strong in project orders, focused on high-temperature segment rather than consumables.

Chinese competition persists in Abrasives and Electrominerals, but is easing with export duty rebate withdrawal and a strong dollar/weak rupee making imports costlier. Electrominerals treated and specialty products are a value-add mix shift.
Foskor Zirconia supply to be replaced by an existing independent source; management says no disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Where is Ceramics growth coming from, and is export growth driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders are the two growth drivers; bare ceramics grew less. Exports are typically 85%+ of Ceramics sales and that ratio held.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AWUKO/Foskor exceptional items arise and are more write-offs expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further AWUKO write-offs are expected; the Foskor exit is on a realisable basis and no extraordinary write-offs are seen, though options are being explored. RHODIUS does not need a write-off.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for standalone Abrasives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views margins as bottomed out at about 10%, with a normal trajectory of 15% to 16%, and is working on pass-through of resin and oil cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow weak and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on strong September sales collected in October-November, and inventory was built for H2 growth. Management expects both to reverse in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue potential exists in semiconductor components and electronic substrates?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor components segment top line of INR 300-350 crores around FY30-31. Electronics substrate timelines are still uncertain; management said at least a year to complete base work and would share later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for RHODIUS?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven targeted by Q1 FY28, followed by small profits. Sales expected flat in FY27 and the loss lower than FY26, after a warehouse move that disrupted the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of VAW Russia volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Status quo: operations remain under the same constraints, with no volume improvement expected in H2.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin compression: standalone PBIT margin near 10% over two quarters; recovery depends on passing through resin and oil-linked cost increases.
Working capital: H1 operating cash flow weak; receivables and inventory build must unwind in H2.
Foskor Zirconia exit and AWUKO liquidation: completion timing and any residual impact; management says none expected.
RHODIUS breakeven target by Q1 FY28; FY27 sales guided flat.
Ceramics growth guidance raised to 25-28%; sustainability depends on Engineered Ceramics and Metallized Cylinders demand.
Chinese import competition in Electrominerals and Abrasives; import pressure may ease with duty changes and currency.
Electronics substrate and armor programs: revenue and timing not yet quantified.
key_quotes: So if you see, our trajectory of margin should be in the range of 15% to 16%, historically, if you take a look at our margins that we have been making, right?

These are specific issues that we are facing largely because of the sudden cost increases, particularly on the phenolic resins, all the oil-based products, and that cost, and of course, you don't stock these items much.
So electronics, we would feel that we should require some more time.
Sridharan Rangarajan: Yes. I think your observation is correct, and this should get reversed in H2, is our view.
We expect the top line from this segment could be somewhere in the range of about INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and demand: management repeatedly stressed record standalone sales, strong Ceramics momentum and raised Ceramics guidance. Cautious and evasive on Abrasives margins (passing through resin and oil costs is still a work in progress), on AWUKO and Foskor write-offs (said "not really" but left options open), and on electronics substrate and armor timelines, which were deferred with no revenue figure.

growth.why: Consolidated FY27 sales guided at ~4-4.5% as reported (11-12% ex-Foskor and AWUKO), with Ceramics growth raised to 25-28% and Abrasives margin cut to 8-8.5% ex-AWUKO; Ceramics growth is backed by demand and new products, while semiconductor and substrate capacity is still years from revenue.
